newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's cold weather death toll climbs to 28.
newsitem.headline: Poland's cold weather death toll climbs to 28.

text.p: A severe cold spell gripping Poland for more than a week has now taken 28 lives, PAP news agency said on Monday.
The frozen body of a 60-year-old man was discovered by police on Monday in the southern mountain village of Jachowka.
Neighbours in the central town of Slubice earlier found 66-year-old Jadwiga P. frozen to death in her unheated home.
Many of the victims of the cold spell, which has sent temperatures plunging as low as -37C (-34F), were apparently drunk when they succumbed to the cold.
Markot, a non-government group which operates Poland's biggest chain of shelters for the homeless, has set up a hotline for information on people threatened by the extreme cold.
Cold weather has killed at least 90 people across Europe in the past week.
Poland's Arctic weather is expected to continue, with lows of -24C (-11F) predicted over the next few days.
